lessons.title: A page is a stack of tags
lessons.blurb: HTML marks up meaning. Every piece of content sits between an opening tag and a closing tag, and the browser turns those tags into things you can see.
notes:
A tag looks like

text

. The slash marks the end.

is the loudest heading on a page.

is a paragraph.
Type in the dark panel. The white panel updates as you type.

lessons.title: Text that carries emphasis
lessons.blurb: Headings run from h1 down to h6, loudest to quietest. Inside a paragraph you can mark words as strong or emphasised, and the browser styles them for you.
notes: <strong> means important. <em> means stressed.

Tags nest:

a bold word

.
Line breaks in your code do not create space on the page.

Flour, water, salt and time.

tasks.label: Wrap one word in <strong>
Wrap another word in <em>
Add an <h2> between the h1 and the h3

lessons.title: Links and images use attributes
lessons.blurb: Some tags need extra information. That goes in attributes inside the opening tag: href says where a link points, src says which image to load, alt describes it in words.
notes: A link: click me
has no closing tag. It carries src and alt instead.
alt text matters: it is what screen readers and broken images show.

tasks.label: Add a link with an href attribute
Give the image different alt text
Make the link open in a new tab with target="_blank"

lessons.title: Lists and tables hold sets
lessons.blurb: When content comes in a set, say so. An unordered list is <ul> with <li> children; a numbered one is <ol>. Tables use rows of <tr> holding <th> headers and <td> cells.
notes: Only <li> belongs directly inside <ul> or <ol>.
A table row lives in <tr>; cells go inside it.
Use a table for real tabular data, never for page layout.

tasks.label: Add a third <li> to the list
Add a numbered <ol> list with at least two items
Add a <table> with a header row and a data row

lessons.title: CSS paints the markup
lessons.blurb: CSS rules pick elements and set properties on them. A rule is a selector, then braces holding property and value pairs. Put your rules inside a style tag.
notes: h1 { color: crimson; } picks every h1 on the page.
font-family sets the typeface; background fills behind an element.
Change a value and watch the preview repaint.

lessons.title: Every element is a box
lessons.blurb: Each element occupies a rectangle: content, then padding inside the edge, then a border, then margin pushing neighbours away. Spacing is mostly choosing these four.
notes: padding is space inside the border, margin is space outside it.
A class targets a group: .card in CSS matches class="card".
border-radius rounds the corners of the box.
lessons.starter_code:

Boxed content.

tasks.label: Add a margin to .card
Round the corners with border-radius

lessons.title: Flexbox arranges children
lessons.blurb: Set display: flex on a container and its children line up along one axis. gap spaces them, justify-content distributes them along the row, align-items lines them up across it.
notes: flex-direction: column stacks the children instead.
gap replaces fiddling with margins between items.
Try justify-content: space-between and see what moves.

lessons.title: Variables remember values
lessons.blurb: JavaScript runs inside a script tag. A variable is a name holding a value: let for something that changes, const for something fixed. Text in quotes joins together with a plus.
notes: document.write is crude, but it shows the result immediately.
Numbers do arithmetic; strings in quotes concatenate.
Every statement usually ends with a semicolon.
lessons.starter_code:
<script>
  const name = "friend";
  let visits = 1;
  document.write("Hello " + name + ", visit number " + visits);
</script>

tasks.label: Change the name value to your own
Declare one more variable
Do some arithmetic, e.g. visits + 1

lessons.title: Reaching into the page
lessons.blurb: The DOM is your HTML as objects JavaScript can touch. Find an element, then read or change it. Hook a function to an event and it runs when the user acts.
notes: document.getElementById("out") finds the element with id="out".
textContent replaces the text inside an element.
addEventListener("click", fn) runs fn on every click.

lessons.title: Choosing between paths
lessons.blurb: An if statement runs a block only when a condition is true, and else covers the rest. Compare with === for equality, or with > and < for size. This is where a page starts making decisions.
notes: === compares, = assigns. Mixing them up is the classic first bug.
else if chains several conditions in order.
Combine conditions with && (and) or || (or).
